1.pericope_label: The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines, before that Pharaoh smote Gaza
debates: Whether the smiting of Gaza is attested in history
Where the name of the city comes from
outliers: Clarke says no historical relation of any Egyptian king smiting Gaza survives in sacred or profane history, while Ellicott treats the attack of Necho as identifiable and dates the prophecy by it
Calvin rejects the derivation of the name from a Persic word for treasures, and the story of Cambyses leaving his riches there, in favour of a Hebrew word meaning strength
themes: False friends on one side and sworn enemies on the other
A ruin foretold while the cities were still in good condition
A first blow that is only the beginning of sorrows
A sword addressed as though it could answer

2.pericope_label: Thus saith the Lord; Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and shall be an overflowing flood, and shall overflow the land, and all that is therein
debates: Who the flood from the north is
What the heading about Pharaoh signifies
Why the fathers abandon their children
outliers: Ellicott takes the flood from the north to rule out Pharaoh-necho and fix the invader as Nebuchadnezzar, while Calvin keeps both, making the Egyptian plunder a prelude and the Chaldean ruin the thing threatened

Ellicott explains the abandoned children as the selfishness of panic crushing natural affection, where Clarke and Calvin make it sheer incapacity, the hands so unstrung that a man cannot move a finger
themes: A flood that turns out to be an army
Goods thrown overboard to buy a life
A road to Egypt kept open behind an army
Men so unstrung that they are like logs of wood

4.pericope_label: Because of the day that cometh to spoil all the Philistines, and to cut off from Tyrus and Zidon every helper that remaineth: for the Lord will spoil the Philistines, the remnant of the country of Caphtor
debates: What the remnant of their valley means
outliers: Clarke has Tyre and Zidon depending on Philistine succour and Ellicott has the two commercial cities employing Philistine mercenaries, while Wesley has Tyre and Sidon called in to help the Philistines

Calvin alone reads the valley as depth and makes the clause a rebuke of false security, where Clarke and Wesley take it of the coastal plain and Ellicott canvasses a Greek reading that gives the remnant of the Anakim instead
themes: Cities that were the defences of a whole country
A coastal plain marked out for desolation
A people called the mere leftovers of Caphtor
Men who thought a deep place would hide them

6.pericope_label: O thou sword of the Lord, how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still
debates: Who speaks the entreaty to the sword
How far the sea shore extends
outliers: Clarke and Wesley give the entreaty to the prophet, Ellicott to the Philistines, and Calvin to the prophet speaking in the character of the Philistines and then reproving himself for it
Calvin reports interpreters who understand the sea shore of Joppa, and prefers to take it of the whole coast, still including Tyre and Sidon and Gaza
themes: A sword told to go back into its scabbard
A weapon that answers the man who addresses it
A commission that cannot be revoked
A sword bound by oath not to stop
